- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent price surged.
- Underestimates mean-reversion zones; if sentiment remains neutral (0.00) and price is above 30-day moving average, slightly lower forecast to align with historical mean.
- Overshoots after volatility spikes (e.g., 75–85 range) — cap forecast at 85% of prior peak or 10% below recent high if sentiment is flat.
- When sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize momentum; add 2–3% downward bias to forecast if last 3 days show consistent decline.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >85% increase from prior 5-day avg), model underreacts — increase forecast by 5–8% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 18-day history — if forecast is heavily influenced by last 3–5 days, reduce weight and average over 30-day window for smoother correction.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, assume no market sentiment bias — apply mean-reversion correction only if price deviates >1.5σ from 30-day mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates late-term price — reduce final 5–7 days by 3–5% if sentiment remains flat and price shows no breakout.
